build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: A sector map shows connected nodes with partial information (icons hinting at combat, shops, or events). The player chooses which node to jump to, spending fuel per jump. Score 0 if no sector map or node choice exists.

Combat shows both ships in cross-section with rooms. The player assigns crew to systems (weapons, shields, engines, medbay) and targets specific enemy rooms. Power distribution between systems is a meaningful choice. Score 0 if no ship combat exists.

Ship systems take damage during combat — damaged systems reduce effectiveness or stop working. Crew can be assigned to repair damaged systems. Fires and hull breaches create additional hazards. Score 0 if no damage system exists.

Fuel and scrap are persistent resources. Fuel limits jumps per sector. Scrap funds repairs, upgrades, and shop purchases. Running out of fuel strands the player. Score 0 if no resource management exists.
Crew members have health and can die permanently. Dead crew cannot be replaced easily. Crew in the medbay heal over time. Losing all crew ends the run. Score 0 if crew are invincible or do not exist.

The full loop connects: title -> sector map -> node encounters -> combat/events -> sector exit -> next sector -> final boss without restarting. Victory and defeat both have result screens. Score 0 if the loop is incomplete or requires relaunch.

At least 3 sectors with procedurally generated node maps, each with increasing difficulty and different encounter distributions. The final sector contains the flagship boss. Score 0 if only one sector exists.

At least 4 distinct encounter types exist: hostile ships (combat), shops (buy/sell), distress signals (risk/reward events), asteroid fields (navigation hazards), and empty beacons. Each resolves differently. Score 0 if only combat encounters exist.

Ship upgrades are available: new weapons, shield improvements, engine boosts, and system additions purchasable at shops or earned from events. At least 5 distinct upgrades exist. Score 0 if no upgrade system exists.

The final boss (flagship) is a multi-phase battle with unique mechanics not seen in regular combat — special weapons, reinforcement waves, or system-disabling attacks. Score 0 if no final boss exists.

Events present narrative choices with risk/reward outcomes — helping a distress signal might yield crew or trigger a trap. At least 5 distinct event scenarios exist with meaningful choices. Score 0 if no events with choices exist.

A styled title screen shows the ship silhouette against a star field. The sector map is clearly readable with node types, connections, and current position. Score 0 if no title or map visualization exists.

The ship cross-section view clearly shows rooms, crew positions, system status (powered/damaged/offline), and hull integrity. During combat, both ships are visible with targeting indicators. Score 0 if no ship view exists.

Resource displays (fuel, scrap, hull HP, crew health) are visible at all times in a clear HUD. System power allocation is readable. Combat damage is shown with visual feedback. Score 0 if no resource display exists.
Readability at 1280x720 is strong: ship rooms, crew, systems, weapons, and map nodes are all clearly distinguishable. Combat state is parseable at a glance. Score 0 if elements blend together.

The art direction is coherent across title, map, ship view, combat, shops, and events — a consistent sci-fi spacefaring aesthetic with unified palette and typography. Score 0 if mostly default UI or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

Ship interiors, crew sprites, weapon effects, and enemy ships use real illustrated or pixel-art assets — not plain ColorRect fills. Different ship types and crew are visually distinct. Score 0 if ships are uniform rectangles.

HUD and UI chrome: resource bars, system panels, shop interfaces, event dialogs, and result screens use styled themed widgets — not raw unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if primary UI elements are obviously unstyled.

Animation and feedback: weapons fire with projectile animations, shields flash on impact, fires flicker in damaged rooms, crew move between rooms, and jumps have a warp transition. Score 0 if all state changes snap silently.
